rubrik: Developing the tax on chemicals in certain electronics
dok_titel: GDP indexation of taxes on chemicals in certain electronics and waste incineration
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:11 by Linus Lakso and Emma Nohrén (both MP).
notis:
The Riksdag said no to the government's proposal to adjust two taxes in relation to the development of gross domestic product (GDP), a so-called GDP indexation. The government's proposal concerns the tax on chemicals in certain electronics and the tax on waste incineration. The change proposed by the government would mean that the taxes are adjusted taking into account both changes in the consumer price index (CPI) and the development of gross domestic product (GDP).
The Riksdag considers that the evaluations carried out of the taxes have shown that they have not been sufficiently effective in achieving the goals that were their purpose. The Riksdag also notes that the government has proposed that the tax on waste incineration be abolished in January 2023. Against this background, the Riksdag said no to the government's proposal to recalculate these taxes based on the GDP index.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:11 by Linus Lakso and Emma Nohrén (both MP).

forslag_text: The Riksdag finally adopts the dormant proposal in Appendix 2 for an act amending the Instrument of Government (regeringsformen).

The Riksdag said yes to a constitutional amendment proposal that entails expanded possibilities to restrict, through ordinary legislation, the freedom of association of organizations that engage in or support terrorism.

rubrik: Amendments to the Code of Judicial Procedure
dok_titel: Foreign espionage (dormant constitutional amendment proposal etc.)
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the government's proposal for an act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure (rättegångsbalken) in the parts concerning Chapter 27, Section 2, and adopts the legislative proposal in other respects with the amendment that
a) 27 Chapter 27, Sections 18, 20 d and 33 shall have the wording proposed by the committee in Appendix 4, 
b) the preamble shall have the wording that follows from this. 
Thereby the Riksdag partially approves Government Bill 2021/22:55 point 4.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposals for legislative amendments and constitutional amendments. The constitutional amendments are a so-called dormant proposal, which means that the Riksdag had already made a decision on that part on a previous occasion.
The legislative proposals mean, among other things, that foreign espionage (utlandsspioneri), aggravated foreign espionage, and aggravated unauthorized handling of secret information based on foreign espionage are criminalized and incorporated into the Penal Code (brottsbalken).
The Riksdag also said yes to the dormant proposal on amendments to the two constitutional laws the Freedom of the Press Act (tryckfrihetsförordningen) and the Fundamental Law on Freedom of Expression (yttrandefrihetsgrundlagen). The amendments mean, among other things, that foreign espionage and those forms of unauthorized handling of secret information and negligent handling of secret information that are based on foreign espionage are also criminalized as press and freedom of expression offences.
The legislative amendments also entail restrictions on the freedom to communicate information and the freedom to procure information (meddelarfriheten and anskaffarfriheten), i.e. the right to communicate and procure information for publication in media forms protected by constitutional law.
Since the proposal in certain parts concerns amendments to constitutional laws, the Riksdag is required to vote identically twice and there must be an election between the votes. The first decision on the constitutional amendment proposal was made on 6 April 2022, when the Riksdag voted yes. Since then there has been a general election.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the government's proposal for an act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure (rättegångsbalken) in the parts concerning Chapter 27, Section 2, and adopts the legislative proposal in other respects with the amendment that
a) Chapter 27, Sections 18, 20 d and 33 shall have the wording proposed by the committee in Appendix 4, 
b) the preamble shall have the wording that follows from this. 
Thereby the Riksdag partially approves Government Bill 2021/22:55 point 4.

rubrik: Amendments to the new Riksbank Act
dok_titel: A new Riksbank Act (dormant constitutional proposals etc.)
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2021/22:4297 by Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) items 1–3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the dormant proposals for amendments to the Instrument of Government (regeringsformen) and the Riksdag Act (riksdagsordningen) concerning the Riksbank, and the Government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act. The proposals for amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Riksdag Act are so-called dormant proposals (vilande förslag), meaning that the Riksdag has previously voted on the matter. The amendments to the Instrument of Government include, among other things, a clarification of the Riksbank's duties. The proposed amendment to the Riksdag Act makes clear that the Riksdag's Committee on Finance shall follow up and evaluate the Riksbank's operations.
The Riksdag also approved the Government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act, but with some minor amendments. The new Riksbank Act entails, among other things:

The Riksbank's objectives, tasks and powers are clarified with regard to monetary policy, the financial system, means of payment, peacetime crisis situations and heightened alert, and international activities
It shall become clearer how the Riksbank's areas of responsibility relate to each other and to those of Finansinspektionen (the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority) and Riksgäldskontoret (the Swedish National Debt Office)
It shall become clearer that the Riksbank, within the framework of monetary policy, shall take real-economic considerations into account, and conditions are created for a democratic anchoring of the specification of the price stability target
The basic structure of the Riksbank's organisation is retained, but the number of members of the Executive Board (direktionen) is reduced from six to five. A more appropriate division of responsibilities is introduced between the General Council (riksbanksfullmäktige), the Executive Board and the Governor (riksbankschefen)
The Riksbank's position as an independent central bank and independent administrative authority is strengthened
The Riksbank's financial independence is strengthened in the framework of, for example, disposing of profits and structuring its own capital, and borrowing for the foreign exchange reserve
The conditions for transparency and scrutiny of the Riksbank's operations are improved
The Riksbank shall contribute to sustainable development in the financial market.

Since the proposals in certain parts concern amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Riksdag Act, the Riksdag is required to vote identically on two occasions with a general election in between. The first decision on the proposals was taken on 1 June 2022, when the Riksdag voted yes. A general election has since taken place.
All legislative amendments are to enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2021/22:4297 by Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) items 1–3.

rubrik: The future regulation of the dispute resolution procedure
dok_titel: An independent dispute resolution procedure for collective rental disputes
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2022/23:13 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) items 1 and 2.
notis:
The previous Government submitted a proposal on dispute resolution in certain collective rental negotiations. This entails, among other things, a new independent dispute resolution body for the entire rental market and tightened rules for rental negotiations.
The parties in the rental market regularly conduct collective negotiations on the general level of rents. Such negotiations are often referred to as the annual rent negotiations. When these negotiations are prolonged, it can entail financial risks for the parties involved.
Within the public housing stock, there is currently a dispute resolution body, the Rental Market Committee (Hyresmarknadskommittén, HMK). A corresponding solution is now to be introduced for the entire rental market, including the private rental stock. If the parties cannot agree on the annual rent adjustment, a special arbitrator may be appointed to examine the dispute. The aim is to make collective negotiations more efficient and for the annual rent negotiations to be concluded more quickly.
Tightened rules for negotiation meetings are also introduced. Among other things, a party may be held liable for damages if it does not attend a negotiation meeting that is to be held within a certain period.
The Riksdag approved the proposal. The new rules enter into force on 1 January 2023.

rubrik: Assignment of coordination numbers to asylum seekers
dok_titel: A strengthened system for coordination numbers
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) item 2.
notis:
The Riksdag endorses the proposal for a new law on coordination numbers (samordningsnummer) and also for amendments to, among other things, the Population Registration Act and the Population Registration Database Act. The purpose is to strengthen the system for coordination numbers by, for example, raising the requirements for the identity checks carried out before a coordination number is issued to a person.
A coordination number is an identity designation for persons who are not, or have not been, registered in Sweden's population register (folkbokförda), but who still need to have contact with Swedish authorities or other parts of society. Persons who are registered in Sweden's population register are instead assigned a personal identity number (personnummer).
Coordination numbers are divided into different levels depending on which identity check was carried out beforehand. Currently there are two levels. Under the new law, a coordination number may be issued at three different levels. To obtain the highest level, the person must be able to prove their identity with valid identity documents and also appear in person at the time of application. The identity documents may also be requested for verification of the biometric data stored in them.
The proposal also means that Skatteverket (the Swedish Tax Agency) takes over responsibility for, among other things, identity checks when a coordination number is to be assigned to a person. Other authorities must notify Skatteverket if it can be assumed that a piece of information in the population registration database is incorrect in relation to persons with coordination numbers.
The proposal also includes a restriction on the exemption from population registration that applies to persons who are locally employed at foreign embassies or consulates in Sweden.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.

dok_titel: A strengthened system for coordination numbers
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) item 4.
notis:
The Riksdag endorses the proposal for a new law on coordination numbers (samordningsnummer) and also for amendments to, among other things, the Population Registration Act and the Population Registration Database Act. The purpose is to strengthen the system for coordination numbers by, for example, raising the requirements for the identity checks carried out before a coordination number is issued to a person.
A coordination number is an identity designation for persons who are not, or have not been, registered in Sweden's population register (folkbokförda), but who still need to have contact with Swedish authorities or other parts of society. Persons who are registered in Sweden's population register are instead assigned a personal identity number (personnummer).
Coordination numbers are divided into different levels depending on which identity check was carried out beforehand. Currently there are two levels. Under the new law, a coordination number may be issued at three different levels. To obtain the highest level, the person must be able to prove their identity with valid identity documents and also appear in person at the time of application. The identity documents may also be requested for verification of the biometric data stored in them.
The proposal also means that Skatteverket (the Swedish Tax Agency) takes over responsibility for, among other things, identity checks when a coordination number is to be assigned to a person. Other authorities must notify Skatteverket if it can be assumed that a piece of information in the population registration database is incorrect in relation to persons with coordination numbers.
The proposal also includes a restriction on the exemption from population registration that applies to persons who are locally employed at foreign embassies or consulates in Sweden.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The legislative amendments concerning those locally employed at embassies and consulates are to enter into force on 1 January 2023, and the remaining ones on 1 September 2023.

an enhanced earned income tax credit (jobbskatteavdrag) for persons over the age of 65
increased tax on alcohol and tobacco
an enhanced tax reduction for the installation of solar panels
a temporary reduction in tax on motor fuels
a reduction in tax on fuels used in certain heat production
a maintained travel expense deduction with certain enhancements for commuting, business travel and home travel.

Some of these proposals have been presented in their own bills, but are announced in the Budget Bill and are included in the revenue estimates for the budget.

rubrik: Subsidiarity review of the Commission's proposal for a regulation establishing a crisis instrument for the internal market
dok_titel: Subsidiarity review of the Commission's proposal for a regulation establishing a crisis instrument for the internal market
forslag_text: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande) to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission, with the wording set out in the committee's proposal in Annex 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has reviewed a legislative proposal from the EU Commission concerning the introduction of an instrument aimed at ensuring that the internal market within the EU — that is, the free movement of persons, goods, and services — functions well even in crisis situations. The proposal also includes provisions on securing the availability of goods and services of strategic importance, which under the proposal is defined as goods and services that are absolutely necessary for the internal market and that cannot be substituted or diversified. The proposal has been reviewed under the so-called subsidiarity principle, which states that the EU should only legislate on an issue if the objectives of the proposed measure cannot be achieved equally well or better by the member states themselves.
The Riksdag considers that the proposal is not in all respects compatible with the subsidiarity principle. According to the Riksdag, there is a need to clarify how the provisions on goods and services of strategic importance relate to the legal basis specified. The Riksdag therefore decided to raise objections to the European Parliament, the Council of Ministers, and the EU Commission in a so-called reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande).
alternatives: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande) to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission, with the wording set out in the committee's proposal in Annex 2.

notes communication 2021/22:241.
notis:
The Riksdag notes that the legitimacy of the annual adjustment of government agency appropriations rests on it being transparent and predictable, and therefore views positively the government's continuous work to increase transparency both in the model itself and in the information about the price and wage adjustment.
Each year, government agencies are allocated appropriations from the state budget to finance, among other things, salaries and premises. Before each new budget year, the Ministry of Finance recalculates the appropriations so that agencies are not affected by price and wage increases in the wider economy.
The price and wage adjustment model (also known as PLO) was introduced approximately 30 years ago and the calculation is carried out automatically so that the state's role as an employer is kept separate from the government's political priorities. In order for agencies to achieve productivity growth in line with the private service sector, a so-called productivity deduction is applied.
It is in response to the Swedish National Audit Office's examination of the PLO and the productivity deduction that the government has submitted a communication (skrivelse). The examination shows, among other things, that the built-in productivity requirement has functioned as a steering signal for efficiency improvements and that it has not prevented agencies from carrying out their mandates.
The Riksdag noted the government's communication, i.e. closed the matter.

The report covers supervision by the Medical Products Agency (Läkemedelsverket), the Health and Social Care Inspectorate (Inspektionen för vård och omsorg, Ivo), and the Dental and Pharmaceutical Benefits Agency (Tandvårds- och läkemedelsförmånsverket, TLV).
The Swedish National Audit Office's conclusion is that the state's supervision of the pharmacy sector and trade in medicines is not effective. This may lead to a situation where both pharmacies and those who buy and sell medicines risk operating in ways that do not meet the requirements of the law. The consequence could then be that patient safety suffers and that expenditure for the state and the regions becomes unnecessarily large.
In the written communication, the Government welcomes the review and takes a positive view of several of the measures proposed by the Swedish National Audit Office. Among other things, the Government considers that there are grounds to consider whether provisions should be introduced to prevent pharmacies from charging excessive prices for medicines not covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme (läkemedelsförmånerna) but subsidised by the state or the regions, and for special dietary foods for children.
The Riksdag largely shares the Government's assessments and considers it essential that supervision can be carried out effectively. With this, the Riksdag noted the written communication, i.e. concluded the matter.

forslag_text:

2022/23:985 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) item 43.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal for amendments to the Agricultural Land Acquisition Act (jordförvärvslagen). The legislative amendments mean that the definition of agricultural property is expanded to cover not only real property classified as an agricultural unit for property assessment purposes but also real property that has been converted or newly formed for the purpose of agriculture or forestry but has not yet been subject to property assessment.
One purpose of the Agricultural Land Acquisition Act is to maintain the balance in land holdings between private individuals and legal entities with regard to agricultural properties. For this reason, a so-called acquisition permit (förvärvstillstånd) is required when legal entities such as a company wish to acquire an agricultural property.
The narrow definition of what constitutes agricultural property has, in several high-profile cases, allowed legal entities to acquire property from natural persons without the provisions on acquisition permits becoming applicable. That is why the Government considers that the rules should be changed.
The new rules are proposed to take effect on 15 April 2023.

rubrik: Emissions trading system in the Baltic Sea
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2022/23:906 by Stina Larsson et al. (C) item 35.
notis:
The Riksdag issued a call — a so-called tillkännagivande (formal directive to the Government) — for expanded investment in wetlands. The call is based on proposals in private members' motion items from the general motions period 2022 on water conservation. The motion items concern expanded efforts to protect and restore existing wetlands and to construct new wetlands. According to the Riksdag, this work needs to continue and be strengthened, as wetlands play a major role in climate action and contribute to, among other things, strengthening biodiversity and counteracting eutrophication in seas and lakes.
The Riksdag voted against the remaining approximately 50 motions from the general motions period 2022, which concern among other things eutrophication, cooperation in the Baltic Sea region, sewage treatment plants, and a marine environment act. The Riksdag considers, among other things, that work is already under way in the areas addressed by the motions.

dok_titel: Results report on development cooperation and humanitarian aid through multilateral organisations
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:849 by Kerstin Lundgren et al. (C) item 55 and 

2022/23:1673 by Annie Lööf et al. (C) item 144.
notis:
Every other year, the Government submits a skrivelse (written communication) with a comprehensive account of development cooperation and humanitarian aid through multilateral organisations — that is, support to international organisations, such as various UN bodies. 
The communication, covering the years 2019 and 2020, shows that the aid channelled through multilateral organisations increased significantly during that period: from approximately 59 percent of the Swedish aid budget in 2019 to approximately 67 percent in 2020.
The Riksdag noted the communication, meaning it closed the matter.
At the same time, the Riksdag voted against consequential motions and eight proposals in motions from the general motions period 2022 concerning multilateral aid, citing ongoing work.
